findings.F1: The book fails on its falls, not on its gain: chained over the windows its deepest fall is 61.5 % against a yearly return of 33.1 % (Calmar 0.54 against 0.75 required), even though its Sharpe of 0.79 beats holding's by 0.24.
findings.F2: The book is in effect a scaled holding of the coins. It holds a position on 98.3 % of coin-days, at a mean allocation of 0.81 when in. Its losing windows match the coins' losing windows: in w2 the book's daily returns sum to -0.39 against the coins' -0.46, in w7 -0.33 against -0.58, and in w14 -0.49 against -0.52. Its chained fall reaches -0.54 in w2, -0.61 in w3 and -0.59 in w4, which is one long fall shared with the coins.
findings.F3: The idea has no edge of its own to offset those falls. Over the 3205 cases the unusual 120-bar move is -0.01 % (t -0.06). The total move is +0.63 %, 3.3 times the 0.19 % round trip, but it is all the coin's normal drift. The unusual move is -0.1 times the cost.
findings.F4: The size of the surge does not grade the move that follows. Across quintiles of the 24-hour return in multiples of its 30-day mean absolute value, the mean unusual move is -0.85 % (t -2.39), +0.63 %, -0.39 %, +0.25 % and +0.20 % (t 0.43), with about 592 cases each. Only the lowest quintile differs from zero, and it is negative.
findings.F5: Nearness to the 30-day high is the situation that separates the surges, though the grading is not smooth across its quintiles:
findings.F6: Surges that come after a deep fall of the previous 7 days do worse. When the 7-day return ending a day before the case is in its lowest quintile (-61 % to -12 %), the unusual 5-day move is -0.93 % (t -1.86, 583 cases), against +0.51 % (t 0.97) in the top quintile.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside, the price keeps rising over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, only while the close stands near its 30-day high: the closer the close to its 30-day high at that hour, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take the surge only when it happens at or near the month's high, and refuse surges that are rebounds inside a month-long decline, which are most of the book's exposure during the coins' shared falls.
ideas.name: surge near monthly high

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside after its 7-day return before that day was a fall, the price rises less than the coin's usual 5-day return over the next 5 days; the deeper that 7-day fall, the larger the shortfall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a sharp up day after a week of heavy selling as a relief bounce to fade or ignore, not a breakout to hold for days.
ideas.name: post-selloff surge fades

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's hourly close stands to its 30-day high, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days compared with its usual 5-day return.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the coin longer and larger the nearer it trades to its month's high, and less as it falls back from it, which keeps the position small inside long declines.
ideas.name: nearness to monthly high
